summary: Barbados admits citizens of most of the world without a visa — the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and the great majority of Commonwealth countries are normally stamped in for up to six months — while CARICOM nationals move freely and every arriving passenger files the online immigration and customs form before landing.

fee.notes: Approximate for a single-entry visitor visa (roughly USD 100); multiple-entry visas cost more. Confirm the current fee with the Barbados mission handling your application.
Individual applicants; a family bundle costs around USD 3,000. Applicants must show annual income of at least USD 50,000 from outside Barbados.
Approximate — the Immigration Department sets extension fees; confirm the current amount before applying in Bridgetown.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for the whole of your intended stay. Airlines often apply a stricter six-month rule, so renew if you are close to expiry.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged one year and over arriving from — or having recently transited — a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. No vaccination is required if you fly in directly from Europe, North America or the rest of the Caribbean.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but visitors pay for private treatment up front and air ambulance transfers are expensive — cover including medical evacuation is strongly recommended.

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed return or onward ticket is expected, along with the address of your accommodation — both are entered on the online immigration form and can be checked on arrival.

proofOfFunds.text: No published minimum. Officers may ask how you will fund your stay, especially for stays of several months.

declarations.name: Barbados online immigration and customs form
declarations.text: Every arriving passenger must complete the free online immigration and customs form at travelform.gov.bb, usually within 72 hours of arrival, and present the QR code at the airport or seaport. There is no charge — do not use paid third-party sites.

currencyLimits.text: Cash or bearer instruments worth BBD 20,000 or more (about USD 10,000) must be declared to Barbados Customs on arrival and departure.

notes: Camouflage-patterned clothing is illegal for civilians in Barbados, including on children. It is confiscated at the airport.
Firearms, ammunition and spear guns require a permit; bringing them in without one is a serious offense.
Fresh fruit, vegetables, plants, meat and dairy are restricted to protect local agriculture. Declare anything you are carrying.

payments.text: Cards work almost everywhere, and US dollars are accepted at the fixed rate of two Barbadian dollars to one US dollar (change usually comes back in Bds$). Keep small notes for buses, rum shops and roadside stalls.

safety.text: Barbados is one of the calmer Caribbean destinations. Petty theft from beaches and parked cars is the main risk, and the Atlantic east coast has powerful currents that are not safe for swimming.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Barbados Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to April is the dry season — sunny, breezy and busiest around Christmas and Easter. Crop Over in July and August is the island's biggest festival, in the middle of the humid, wetter half of the year.

idp.text: Barbados is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Barbados is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Barbados yet.

tips.text: Do not pack camouflage clothing — wearing or importing camouflage patterns is illegal for civilians in Barbados, and items are taken off travelers at the airport, including children's clothes.
Complete the free online immigration and customs form at travelform.gov.bb within 72 hours of arrival and save the QR code offline. Third-party sites charging for it are not official.

Visitors need a Barbados visitor's driving permit, issued by car rental firms and police stations on presentation of a valid license. Driving is on the left, and rural roads are narrow with deep gutters.
Barbados tap water comes from filtered coral limestone aquifers and is safe and pleasant to drink — refill a bottle rather than buying plastic.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Barbados?
faq.answer: Most travelers do not. Citizens of the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, the EU and the great majority of Commonwealth countries enter without a visa and are normally stamped in for up to six months. CARICOM nationals move freely. If your nationality is not exempt, apply to a Barbados high commission, embassy or consulate before traveling.

faq.question: Do I need to fill in the Barbados travel form?
faq.answer: Yes. Every arriving passenger must complete the online immigration and customs form at travelform.gov.bb, normally within 72 hours before arrival, and show the QR code on landing. It is free — ignore sites that charge for it.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Barbados?
faq.answer: Visa-free visitors are usually granted up to six months, though the officer decides based on your ticket and plans. Extensions are handled by the Immigration Department in Bridgetown for a fee, and must be requested before your current stamp expires.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from Barbados?
faq.answer: Yes. The Barbados Welcome Stamp allows remote workers to live on the island for 12 months, renewable. It costs around USD 2,000 for an individual (about USD 3,000 for a family bundle) and requires annual income of at least USD 50,000 earned outside Barbados.

faq.question: Can I use US dollars in Barbados?
faq.answer: Yes. The Barbadian dollar is pegged at two to one US dollar, and US cash is widely accepted, but change is normally given in Barbadian dollars. Cards are accepted nearly everywhere, so most visitors need very little cash.
